title: Build release notes edit flow and approval lattice
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Create a deterministic, auditable edit-and-approval workflow for release notes that produces both an internal changelog (detailed engineering and rollout notes) and a concise customer-facing changelog (tiered messages by customer segment). This ticket consolidates the edit queue, defines role-based approval gates, and produces ready-to-publish artefacts for the release lead and comms team.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical draft (document + version history) exists for each release and is stored in the Release Notes repo/Confluence page.
At least two approval lanes are enforceable: internal (engineering/product) and external/copy (comms/legal) with timestamped approvals.
Customer-facing changelog can be generated as a 3-tier summary (Public blog blurb, Customer portal summary, Enterprise customer bulletin) from the canonical draft without manual copy-paste.
Editorial owners can triage and assign incoming change entries via a triage queue within the Console release checklist.
Rollout checklist includes explicit rollback messaging and known issues with linkable incident runbooks.
All metadata fields (author, impact, component, doc link, PR link) are present for each changelog line item.
A handoff checklist for Sales/CS is produced automatically and published to the shared Drive folder.
Metrics: time from draft creation to customer-publish reduced to <= 72 hours for minor releases and <= 7 days for major releases in the next two sprints.

open_questions: What is the minimal set of metadata we require to populate all three customer tiers automatically?
Do we enforce approvals for release notes that are 'informational only' and how is that classification defined?
Can we surface changelog drafts inside the Console release checklist without exposing sensitive rollout details to all org members?
